Medicine-02.question: ১) In a hypertensive patient, which type of apex beat typically found?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is heaving apex beat. In hypertension, chronic pressure overload causes left ventricular hypertrophy, producing a sustained/heaving apex beat.

Key points:

  • Hypertension → Increased afterload → LV pressure overload → LV hypertrophy

  • LV hypertrophy causes:

    • Heaving (sustained) apex beat

    • Often displaced laterally if severe

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Thrusting apex beat → Usually refers to a forceful but less sustained impulse; may be seen in hyperdynamic states.

  • Dyskinetic apex beat → Suggests ventricular aneurysm or abnormal ventricular wall movement.

  • Normal → Not expected in significant hypertensive LV hypertrophy.

High-yield clinical examination:

Condition Apex beat
Hypertension (LVH) Heaving/sustained
Aortic stenosis Heaving
Dilated cardiomyopathy Displaced, diffuse
Hyperdynamic states Thrusting

Exam pearl:
Hypertension → LVH → Heaving apex beat.

Medicine-02.question: ২) Absent a wave in JVP is found in which of the following condition?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is atrial fibrillation. The a wave in JVP represents right atrial contraction; it disappears when there is no effective atrial contraction, as in atrial fibrillation.

JVP waves:

  • a wave → Right atrial contraction

  • c wave → Tricuspid valve bulging during ventricular contraction

  • v wave → Right atrial filling during ventricular systole

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tricuspid regurgitation → Causes large v waves due to systolic backflow of blood into the right atrium.

  • ASD → Usually causes increased flow and may produce a prominent pulmonary flow murmur; a waves are not typically absent.

  • VSD → Does not cause absent a waves.

High-yield JVP findings:

Condition JVP finding
Atrial fibrillation Absent a wave
Complete heart block Cannon a waves
Tricuspid stenosis Giant a waves
Tricuspid regurgitation Giant v waves

Exam pearl:
Absent a wave = absent atrial contraction → Atrial fibrillation.

Medicine-02.question: ৩) Regarding Hemodynamic effects during inspiration, which information is correct?
Medicine-02.exp: Explanation

Medicine-02.question: ৪) In a 12-lead ECG, P wave represents..
৫) Which of the following feature is closely related to left heart failure?
Medicine-02.exp: Explanation:

Medicine-02.question: ৬) Which of the following feature is closely related to Right heart failure?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is peripheral pitting oedema. Right heart failure causes systemic venous congestion, leading to fluid accumulation in dependent tissues and peripheral oedema.

Key features of right heart failure:

  • Raised JVP

  • Peripheral pitting oedema

  • Hepatomegaly

  • Ascites

  • Weight gain due to fluid retention

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Pleural effusions → Can occur in both right and left heart failure but are less specific.

  • Pulmonary oedema → Mainly a feature of left heart failure due to pulmonary venous congestion.

  • Cardiomegaly → May occur in both types of heart failure; not specific for right heart failure.

High-yield heart failure recall:

Type Main feature
Left heart failure Pulmonary oedema
Right heart failure Peripheral pitting oedema + raised JVP

Exam pearl:
Right heart failure → systemic venous congestion → peripheral oedema.

Medicine-02.question: ৭) Physiological cause of bradycardia is?
Medicine-02.exp: Explanation:

Medicine-02.question: ৮) Pathological causes of trachcardia is..
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is fever. Fever causes pathological tachycardia due to increased metabolic demand and sympathetic stimulation.

Key points:

  • Fever increases heart rate approximately 10 beats/min for each 1°C rise in body temperature (approximate).

  • Mechanism:

    • ↑ Metabolic demand

    • ↑ Sympathetic activity

    • ↑ Cardiac output requirement

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Exercise → Physiological tachycardia.

  • Emotion → Physiological tachycardia due to sympathetic activation.

  • Pregnancy → Physiological tachycardia due to increased blood volume and cardiac output.

High-yield recall:

Physiological tachycardia: Exercise, emotion, pregnancy
Pathological tachycardia: Fever, anaemia, thyrotoxicosis, heart failure

Exam pearl:
Fever → pathological sinus tachycardia.

Medicine-02.question: ৯) What is the most important modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is smoking. Smoking is the most important modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD) because it accelerates atherosclerosis and increases thrombotic risk.

Effects of smoking:

  • Endothelial injury

  • Increased LDL oxidation

  • Increased platelet activation

  • Coronary thrombosis risk

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Age and sex → Important non-modifiable risk factors.

  • Alcohol → Heavy alcohol intake may increase cardiovascular risk, but it is not the most important modifiable CAD risk factor.

  • Hypertension → A major modifiable risk factor, but smoking is traditionally considered the strongest preventable risk factor for CAD.

High-yield CAD risk factors:

Non-modifiable: Age, sex, family history
Modifiable: Smoking, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, obesity

Exam pearl:
Most important modifiable risk factor for CAD = Smoking.

Medicine-02.question: ১০) A patient with severe chest pain for 30 minutes, waht will be the most initial investigation?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is 12-lead ECG. In a patient with severe chest pain lasting 30 minutes (suspected acute coronary syndrome), a 12-lead ECG is the first investigation and should be performed urgently.

Key points:

  • 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of presentation in suspected ACS.

  • It identifies:

    • ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)

    • ST depression/T-wave changes

    • Arrhythmias

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Echocardiography → Useful for assessing wall motion abnormalities and complications, but not the initial test.

  • Exercise ECG → Contraindicated in acute severe chest pain/suspected ACS.

  • Troponin I → Important biomarker for myocardial injury, but may be negative early and does not replace the initial ECG.

High-yield ACS approach:

Chest pain suggestive of ACS → 12-lead ECG first → Troponin → Further management

Exam pearl:
First investigation in suspected acute MI = 12-lead ECG.

Medicine-02.question: ১১) Acute coronary syndrome includes all of the following, except...
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is stable angina. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) includes unstable angina, STEMI, and NSTEMI; stable angina is a chronic form of ischaemic heart disease, not ACS.

Components of ACS:

  • Unstable angina

  • ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)

  • Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Unstable angina → Part of ACS.

  • ST-elevated MI (STEMI) → Part of ACS.

  • Non-ST-elevated MI (NSTEMI) → Part of ACS.

High-yield ACS recall:

ACS = UA + NSTEMI + STEMI
Stable angina = Chronic coronary syndrome (not ACS)

Exam pearl:
Stable angina is excluded from acute coronary syndrome.

Medicine-02.question: ১২) Acute coronary syndrome almost always occurs in patients who have which of the following condition?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is atherosclerosis. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) almost always occurs due to rupture of an atherosclerotic coronary plaque with subsequent thrombus formation.

Pathogenesis of ACS:

  • Atherosclerotic plaque formation

  • Plaque rupture/erosion

  • Platelet activation and thrombus formation

  • Acute reduction in coronary blood flow

The other options are incorrect because:

  • DM → A major risk factor for atherosclerosis, but not the direct underlying condition causing ACS.

  • HTN → A risk factor that accelerates atherosclerosis.

  • Valvular heart disease → Not a usual cause of ACS.

High-yield ACS recall:

ACS = Atherosclerotic plaque rupture + coronary thrombosis

Exam pearl:
Underlying pathology of ACS = coronary atherosclerosis.

Medicine-02.question: ১৩) What is the earliest change of ECG folloing Myoardial infraction?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is ST segment elevation. The earliest ECG change following acute myocardial infarction (especially STEMI) is ST-segment elevation due to acute myocardial injury.

Sequence of ECG changes after MI:

  1. ST segment elevation → Earliest change (minutes)

  2. Hyperacute T waves

  3. T wave inversion

  4. Pathological Q waves

The other options are incorrect because:

  • T inversion → Occurs later due to myocardial ischaemia.

  • Q wave change → Indicates myocardial necrosis and develops later (hours to days).

  • ST-segment deviation → A general term; the specific earliest change is ST-segment elevation in acute transmural MI.

High-yield ECG in MI:

ST elevation → T inversion → Q wave formation

Exam pearl:
Earliest ECG change in acute MI = ST segment elevation.

Medicine-02.question: ১৪) Normal systolic Blood pressure is..
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is <120 mmHg. Normal systolic blood pressure is defined as less than 120 mmHg in adults.

Blood pressure classification (adult):

Category Systolic BP
Normal <120 mmHg
Elevated 120–129 mmHg
Hypertension ≥130 mmHg

The other options are incorrect because:

  • <130 mmHg → Includes elevated BP range.

  • 120–139 mmHg → Above normal range (elevated/pre-hypertensive range).

  • 130–139 mmHg → Stage 1 hypertension range.

Exam pearl:
Normal systolic BP = <120 mmHg.

Medicine-02.question: ১৫) Which antihypertensive is contraindicated in pregnancy?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is ACE inhibitors. ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy because they can cause fetal renal impairment, oligohydramnios, skull abnormalities, and fetal death, especially in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • β-blockers → Some (e.g., labetalol) are commonly used and considered safe in pregnancy.

  • Calcium channel blockers → Nifedipine is commonly used for hypertension in pregnancy.

  • All above → Incorrect because β-blockers and calcium channel blockers are not contraindicated.

High-yield hypertension in pregnancy:

Preferred drugs:

  • Labetalol

  • Nifedipine

  • Methyldopa

Contraindicated:

  • ACE inhibitors

  • ARBs

  • Direct renin inhibitors

Exam pearl:
Pregnancy + ACE inhibitor = contraindicated.

Medicine-02.question: ১৬) which one of the following is a Minor manifestation of rheumatic fever.
১৭) Which one of the following is pathognomonic for rheumatic fever?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is Aschoff nodules. Aschoff bodies (nodules) are the characteristic histopathological lesion of rheumatic fever and are considered pathognomonic.

Key points:

  • Aschoff bodies consist of:

    • Central area of fibrinoid necrosis

    • Anitschkow cells ("caterpillar cells")

    • Lymphocytes and plasma cells

  • Found mainly in the myocardium in rheumatic carditis.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Chorea → A major Jones criterion but not pathognomonic.

  • Erythema marginatum → A major Jones criterion but not specific.

  • Subcutaneous nodules → A major Jones criterion but not pathognomonic.

High-yield rheumatic fever recall:

Pathognomonic lesion = Aschoff body (nodule)
Most specific clinical feature = Sydenham chorea

Exam pearl:
Rheumatic fever histology → Aschoff nodules.

Medicine-02.question: ১৮) In a patient with Chronic rheumatic heart disease, which valve is mostly affected?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is mitral valve. The mitral valve is the most commonly affected valve in chronic rheumatic heart disease (CRHD).

Key points:

  • Rheumatic heart disease mainly affects the left-sided valves.

  • Common valve involvement:

    1. Mitral valve (most common)

    2. Aortic valve

    3. Tricuspid valve (rare)

    4. Pulmonary valve (very rare)

Chronic rheumatic mitral valve disease commonly causes:

  • Mitral stenosis

  • Mitral regurgitation

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tricuspid → Less commonly affected.

  • Aortic → Second most commonly affected.

  • Pulmonary → Rarely involved.

High-yield rheumatic heart disease recall:

Most common valve affected = Mitral valve
Most common lesion in chronic rheumatic heart disease = Mitral stenosis

Exam pearl:
Rheumatic fever → Mitral valve involvement is most common.

Medicine-02.question: ১৯) Loud first heart sound, opening snap, Mid-diastolic murmur. These are the feature of which type of vulvular heat disease?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is mitral stenosis. Loud first heart sound (S1), opening snap, and mid-diastolic rumbling murmur are classic features of mitral stenosis.

Key clinical features of mitral stenosis:

  • Loud S1 → Due to forceful closure of stenosed mitral valve

  • Opening snap → Sudden opening of stiff mitral valve

  • Mid-diastolic murmur → Low-pitched rumbling murmur at apex

  • Best heard with patient in left lateral position

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tricuspid stenosis → Similar diastolic murmur but usually associated with right-sided signs and is much less common.

  • Aortic stenosis → Causes systolic ejection murmur, slow-rising pulse.

  • Pulmonary stenosis → Causes systolic ejection murmur in pulmonary area.

High-yield valvular recall:

Mitral stenosis = Loud S1 + Opening snap + Mid-diastolic rumbling murmur

Exam pearl:
Opening snap + mid-diastolic murmur = Mitral stenosis.

Medicine-02.question: ২০) Which of the following is the preferred investigation for vulvular heat disease?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is echocardiography. Echocardiography is the preferred investigation for valvular heart disease because it provides direct assessment of valve structure, severity of lesions, and haemodynamic effects.

Uses of echocardiography:

  • Valve morphology

  • Severity of stenosis/regurgitation

  • Chamber size and function

  • Pulmonary artery pressure

  • Doppler assessment of blood flow

The other options are incorrect because:

  • ECG → May show chamber hypertrophy or rhythm abnormalities but does not assess valve lesions directly.

  • ETT (Exercise tolerance test) → Used for functional assessment, especially in selected patients.

  • CT chest → Not the primary investigation for valvular disease.

High-yield valvular disease recall:

Best investigation for valvular heart disease = Echocardiography (Doppler echo)

Exam pearl:
Valve lesion assessment → Echocardiogram.

Medicine-02.question: ২১) Which one of following is the the most common cause of acute endocarditis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is Staphylococcus aureus. S. aureus is the most common cause of acute infective endocarditis, especially in patients with normal valves, intravenous drug use, and prosthetic valves.

Common organisms causing infective endocarditis:

Type Common organism
Acute endocarditis Staphylococcus aureus
Subacute endocarditis Viridans streptococci
Prosthetic valve (early) Staphylococcus epidermidis
IV drug users Staphylococcus aureus
Colonic lesion association Streptococcus gallolyticus

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Enterococcus spp. → Can cause IE, often associated with urinary/GI sources, but less common.

  • Viridans streptococci → Classical cause of subacute infective endocarditis.

  • Strep. gallolyticus → Associated with colonic neoplasia and endocarditis.

High-yield infective endocarditis recall:

Acute IE = Staphylococcus aureus
Subacute IE = Viridans streptococci

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of acute endocarditis → Staph. aureus.

Medicine-02.question: ২২) Which of the following is the pivotal investigation for infective endocarditis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is blood culture. Blood culture is the pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis because it identifies the causative organism and guides antibiotic therapy.

Key points:

  • Take 3 sets of blood cultures from separate venepuncture sites before starting antibiotics (if patient is stable).

  • Helps identify:

    • Causative organism

    • Antibiotic sensitivity

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Echocardiography → Important for detecting vegetations, valve damage, and complications, but it does not identify the organism.

  • ECG → May show conduction abnormalities but is not diagnostic.

  • ETT → Not used for diagnosis of infective endocarditis.

High-yield infective endocarditis recall:

Diagnosis = Blood culture + Echocardiography (Modified Duke criteria)

Exam pearl:
Pivotal investigation for infective endocarditis = Blood culture.

Medicine-02.question: ২৩) ST elevation with upward concavity & PR interval depression is diagnostic for?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is acute pericarditis. Diffuse ST-segment elevation with upward concavity and PR interval depression are classic ECG features of acute pericarditis.

ECG features of acute pericarditis:

  • Diffuse ST elevation (concave upward)

  • PR segment depression

  • Usually widespread except aVR (may show ST depression and PR elevation)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Chronic pericarditis → Usually does not produce these acute inflammatory ECG changes.

  • Pericardial effusion → May show low-voltage QRS and electrical alternans if large.

  • Cardiac tamponade → May show electrical alternans, tachycardia, and low voltage, but not typical diffuse ST elevation with PR depression.

High-yield ECG recall:

Acute pericarditis = Diffuse ST elevation + PR depression

Exam pearl:
ST elevation with upward concavity + PR depression → Acute pericarditis.

Medicine-02.question: ২৪) Which one is not appropriate finding on bed side examination of pneumonia patient?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is percussion – hyper-resonant. In pneumonia, lung consolidation produces a dull percussion note, not a hyper-resonant note.

Typical bedside findings in lobar pneumonia:

  • Bronchial breath sounds ✓ (due to consolidated lung transmitting airway sounds)

  • Increased vocal resonance ✓ (increased transmission through solid lung)

  • Dull percussion note ✓ (due to fluid-filled/consolidated alveoli)

  • Tachypnoea ✓ (due to respiratory distress)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Bronchial breath sounds → Classical sign of lung consolidation.

  • Increased vocal resonance → Seen in consolidation.

  • Tachypnoea → Common clinical feature of pneumonia.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Pneumonia with consolidation:

  • Percussion → Dull

  • Breath sound → Bronchial

  • Vocal resonance → Increased

Exam pearl:
Hyper-resonance suggests air trapping (e.g., pneumothorax/emphysema), not pneumonia.

Medicine-02.question: ২৫) Productive cough, changes in posture induce sputum production is a feature of
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is bronchiectasis. A chronic productive cough with large amounts of sputum that increases with changes in posture is a classic feature of bronchiectasis.

Key features of bronchiectasis:

  • Chronic productive cough

  • Copious purulent sputum

  • Postural variation in sputum production (sputum drains from dilated bronchi when position changes)

  • Recurrent chest infections

  • Coarse crackles on auscultation

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tuberculosis → May cause chronic cough and sputum, but postural sputum production is not a typical feature.

  • Pneumonia → Usually presents acutely with fever, productive cough, and systemic symptoms.

  • Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) → Chronic productive cough occurs, but posture-related large sputum production is more characteristic of bronchiectasis.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Bronchiectasis = Chronic productive cough + copious sputum + postural drainage

Exam pearl:
Posture-induced sputum production → Bronchiectasis.

Medicine-02.question: ২৬) The accumulation of serous fluid within the pleural space is termed as..
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is pleural effusion. Accumulation of serous fluid within the pleural space is termed pleural effusion.

Types of pleural fluid accumulation:

  • Pleural effusion → Serous fluid accumulation

  • Empyema → Pus/infected pleural fluid

  • Haemothorax → Blood in pleural space

  • Chylothorax → Lymphatic (chyle) accumulation due to thoracic duct leakage

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Empyema → Collection of pus, usually due to infection.

  • Haemothorax → Collection of blood, commonly after trauma.

  • Chylothorax → Collection of milky lymphatic fluid.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Serous fluid in pleural space = Pleural effusion
Pus = Empyema | Blood = Haemothorax | Chyle = Chylothorax

Exam pearl:
Pleural effusion = abnormal accumulation of fluid in pleural cavity.

Medicine-02.question: ২৭) Which one of the following causes unilateral pleural effusion?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is malignant disease. Malignant pleural effusion is commonly unilateral due to local pleural involvement by tumour.

Causes of unilateral pleural effusion:

  • Malignancy (lung cancer, breast cancer, metastasis)

  • Pulmonary embolism/infarction

  • Pneumonia (parapneumonic effusion)

  • Tuberculosis

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Cardiac failure → Usually causes bilateral pleural effusions due to increased hydrostatic pressure.

  • Pulmonary infarction → Can cause unilateral effusion, but is less common than malignancy in this context.

  • Nephrotic syndrome → Usually causes bilateral effusions due to hypoalbuminaemia.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Unilateral pleural effusion → Think malignancy, TB, PE, pneumonia
Bilateral pleural effusion → Think heart failure, nephrotic syndrome, hypoalbuminaemia

Exam pearl:
Most important cause of unilateral pleural effusion = Malignancy.

Medicine-02.question: ২৮) Which one of the following is an example of transudative pleural effusion?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is cardiac failure. Transudative pleural effusion occurs due to systemic factors that alter hydrostatic or oncotic pressure, and heart failure is the most common cause.

Causes of transudative pleural effusion:

  • Congestive cardiac failure (most common)

  • Cirrhosis with portal hypertension

  • Nephrotic syndrome

  • Hypoalbuminaemia

The other options are incorrect because they cause exudative pleural effusion:

  • Tuberculosis → Exudative effusion due to inflammation.

  • Malignant disease → Exudative effusion due to increased vascular permeability or lymphatic obstruction.

  • Rheumatoid disease → Exudative effusion due to inflammatory pleuritis.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Transudate = Pressure problem

  • Heart failure

  • Cirrhosis

  • Nephrotic syndrome

Exudate = Pleural disease

  • Infection (TB, pneumonia)

  • Malignancy

  • Autoimmune disease

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of transudative pleural effusion = Cardiac failure.

Medicine-02.question: ২৯) Example of Chronic type-1 Repiratory failure is..
Medicine-02.exp: Explanation:

Medicine-02.question: ৩০) Example of Acute type-2 Repiratory failure is..
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is acute severe asthma. Acute type 2 respiratory failure occurs when there is hypoxaemia with hypercapnia (raised PaCO₂) due to inadequate ventilation.

Acute type 2 respiratory failure examples:

  • Acute severe asthma (due to severe airflow obstruction and ventilatory failure)

  • Acute exacerbation of COPD

  • Neuromuscular weakness

  • Drug overdose causing respiratory depression

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Lobar collapse → Usually causes type 1 respiratory failure (V/Q mismatch).

  • Pneumothorax → Usually causes type 1 respiratory failure due to impaired oxygenation.

  • Pulmonary embolus → Causes type 1 respiratory failure due to ventilation-perfusion mismatch.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Type ABG pattern Examples
Type 1 ↓ PaO₂, normal/↓ PaCO₂ Pneumonia, PE, pulmonary oedema
Type 2 ↓ PaO₂ + ↑ PaCO₂ Acute severe asthma, COPD exacerbation

Exam pearl:
Acute severe asthma → Acute type 2 respiratory failure.

Medicine-02.question: ৩১) A diurnal variation in PEF of more than 20% is considered diagnostic of which of the following condition?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is bronchial asthma. A diurnal variation in peak expiratory flow (PEF) of more than 20% is characteristic of asthma due to variable and reversible airway obstruction.

Key points:

  • PEF variability >20% → Suggests asthma

  • Asthma shows:

    • Variable airflow limitation

    • Diurnal variation (often worse at night/early morning)

    • Reversibility with bronchodilator

The other options are incorrect because:

  • COPD → Causes persistent airflow limitation with less day-to-day variability.

  • Lung fibrosis → Restrictive lung disease; does not cause significant PEF variation.

  • Empyema → Pleural infection; not associated with PEF variability.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Asthma diagnosis:

  • ↑ PEF variability (>20%)

  • Bronchodilator reversibility

  • Variable symptoms (wheeze, cough, breathlessness)

Exam pearl:
PEF diurnal variation >20% = Bronchial asthma.

Medicine-02.question: ৩২) Which of the following is not a feature of Acute severe asthma?
Medicine-02.option4: Inability to complete sentences in 1 breath
Medicine-02.exp:
Explanation:

The correct answer is respiratory rate ≥15 breaths/min. A respiratory rate of 15/min is not a feature of acute severe asthma; severe asthma usually causes marked tachypnoea.

Features of acute severe asthma (BTS/SIGN criteria):

  • PEF 33–50% predicted (or <200 L/min)

  • Heart rate ≥110 beats/min

  • Respiratory rate ≥25 breaths/min

  • Unable to complete sentences in one breath

The other options are correct features:

  • PEF 33–50% predicted (<200 L/min) ✓ → Acute severe asthma.

  • Heart rate ≥110 beats/min ✓ → Due to respiratory distress and sympathetic activation.

  • Inability to complete sentences in one breath ✓ → Indicates severe airflow obstruction.

High-yield asthma severity recall:

Acute severe asthma:

  • PEF 33–50%

  • RR ≥25/min

  • HR ≥110/min

  • Speech limited to phrases

Exam pearl:
RR ≥15/min is normal range, not a marker of acute severe asthma.

Medicine-02.question: ৩৩) Which teratment option is central to the management of breathlessness in a COPD patient?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is bronchodilator. Bronchodilators are central to the management of breathlessness in COPD because they reduce airway obstruction and improve airflow.

Key points:

  • Mainstay treatment for COPD symptoms:

    • Short-acting bronchodilators (for relief)

    • Long-acting bronchodilators (for maintenance)

  • Classes:

    • β₂-agonists

    • Antimuscarinics

The other options are incorrect because:

  • O₂ inhalation → Used in patients with chronic hypoxaemia, not as the primary treatment for breathlessness in all COPD patients.

  • Oral glucocorticoids → Mainly used during acute exacerbations, not for routine symptom control.

  • Pulmonary rehabilitation → Important for improving exercise capacity and quality of life but not the primary pharmacological treatment of breathlessness.

High-yield COPD recall:

COPD breathlessness → Bronchodilator is the cornerstone therapy

Exam pearl:
First-line symptomatic treatment for COPD dyspnoea = Bronchodilator.

Medicine-02.question: ৩৪) Which of the following is the most common cause of Brochiectasis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is pulmonary tuberculosis. In many developing countries, including Bangladesh, pulmonary tuberculosis is one of the most common causes of acquired bronchiectasis due to chronic airway destruction and fibrosis.

Causes of bronchiectasis:

  • Post-tuberculous bronchiectasis (common in TB-endemic regions)

  • Severe childhood respiratory infections

  • Cystic fibrosis

  • Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA)

  • Immunodeficiency

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Suppurative pneumonia → Can cause bronchiectasis, especially after severe childhood infections, but less commonly than TB in endemic areas.

  • Lung abscess → May cause localized bronchial damage but is not the commonest cause.

  • Empyema → Pleural infection; not a common cause of bronchiectasis.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Bronchiectasis causes:

  • Post-infectious (TB, severe pneumonia)

  • Cystic fibrosis

  • ABPA

  • Immune deficiency

Exam pearl:
In TB-endemic areas → Pulmonary tuberculosis is a common cause of bronchiectasis.

Medicine-02.question: ৩৫) Investigation of choise for Brochiectasis
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is HRCT (High-resolution CT chest). HRCT is the investigation of choice for diagnosing bronchiectasis because it directly demonstrates bronchial dilatation and structural airway changes.

HRCT findings:

  • Bronchial dilatation (bronchus wider than accompanying artery → signet ring sign)

  • Lack of bronchial tapering

  • Bronchial wall thickening

  • Bronchial visibility close to pleura

The other options are incorrect because:

  • CXR → May show suggestive features but has low sensitivity.

  • MRI → Not routinely used for bronchiectasis assessment.

  • Bronchoscopy → Used to identify obstruction, foreign body, or obtain samples, not the primary diagnostic test.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Bronchiectasis → Investigation of choice = HRCT chest

Exam pearl:
Best diagnostic test for bronchiectasis = HRCT.

Medicine-02.question: ৩৬) Acute coryza is the most common URTI and is usually the result of which of the following organism?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is Rhinovirus. Acute coryza (common cold) is the most common upper respiratory tract infection and is most commonly caused by rhinoviruses.

Key points:

  • Rhinovirus → Most common cause of common cold (acute coryza)

  • Other viral causes:

    • Coronavirus

    • Adenovirus

    • Respiratory syncytial virus

The other options are incorrect because:

  • S. aureus → Causes bacterial infections such as skin infection, pneumonia, and endocarditis.

  • S. pneumoniae → Causes bacterial pneumonia, otitis media, and sinusitis.

  • H. influenzae → Causes otitis media, sinusitis, and lower respiratory infections.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Acute coryza/common cold = Rhinovirus

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of URTI = Rhinovirus.

Medicine-02.question: ৩৮) Which of the following is the most common infecting agent causing Community-acquired pneumonia?

Medicine-02.question: ৩৯) Which one isn’t correct regarding CURB-65 score of pneumonia?
Medicine-02.option4: Blood pressure (systolic < 90 mmHg or diastolic < 60 mmHg)

Medicine-02.question: ৪০) What is the Common complication of pneumonia?
Medicine-02.option3: Retention of sputum causing lobar collapse
Medicine-02.option4: Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Medicine-02.exp:
Explanation:

The correct answer is para-pneumonic effusion. It is the most common complication of pneumonia, occurring due to inflammation spreading from the infected lung to the pleural space.

Complications of pneumonia:

  • Para-pneumonic effusion (most common)

  • Empyema (infected pleural fluid)

  • Lung abscess

  • Sepsis

  • Respiratory failure

The other options are less appropriate:

  • Empyema → A complication of pneumonia but less common than para-pneumonic effusion.

  • Retention of sputum causing lobar collapse → Can occur but is not a common complication.

  • Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism → Not a typical direct complication of pneumonia.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Common complication of pneumonia = Para-pneumonic effusion
Infected pleural effusion = Empyema

Exam pearl:
Pneumonia → pleural effusion is the commonest complication.

Medicine-02.question: ৪১) Which one is the most common extra pulmonary site of Tuberculosis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is lymph node. Tuberculous lymphadenitis is the most common form of extra-pulmonary tuberculosis.

Common sites of extra-pulmonary TB:

  1. Lymph nodes (most common)

  2. Pleura

  3. Bone and joints

  4. CNS (TB meningitis)

  5. Intestine

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Brain → Important site causing TB meningitis, but not the most common.

  • Intestine → Can occur, especially with swallowed infected sputum, but less common.

  • Bone → Causes osteoarticular TB (e.g., Pott disease), but less common.

High-yield TB recall:

Most common extra-pulmonary TB = Lymph node
Most common site of TB overall = Lung

Exam pearl:
TB lymphadenitis is the commonest extra-pulmonary manifestation of tuberculosis.

Medicine-02.question: ৪২) Night sweats is a clinical feature of which of the following condition?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is infective endocarditis. Night sweats are a classic constitutional symptom of infective endocarditis due to chronic infection and inflammatory cytokine release.

Clinical features of infective endocarditis:

  • Fever

  • Night sweats

  • Fatigue and weight loss

  • New or changing heart murmur

  • Embolic phenomena

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Heart failure → Causes breathlessness, orthopnoea, oedema, and fatigue; night sweats are not typical.

  • Cardiac tamponade → Causes hypotension, raised JVP, muffled heart sounds (Beck’s triad).

  • Enteric fever → Causes prolonged fever and systemic symptoms, but night sweats are classically associated with infective endocarditis and TB.

High-yield recall:

Night sweats + fever + murmur → Infective endocarditis

Exam pearl:
Classic cardiac condition associated with night sweats = Infective endocarditis.

Medicine-02.question: ৪৩) Which one is the gold standard investigation for Tuberculosis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is culture. Mycobacterial culture is considered the gold standard investigation for tuberculosis because it provides definitive diagnosis and allows drug susceptibility testing.

Key points:

  • Culture (solid or liquid media):

    • Highest specificity

    • Allows antimicrobial sensitivity testing

    • Takes longer (weeks)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • CXR → Useful for detecting suggestive radiological changes but cannot confirm TB.

  • NAAT (e.g., GeneXpert MTB/RIF) → Rapid and highly useful for diagnosis and rifampicin resistance detection, but traditionally not the gold standard.

  • CT → Provides detailed imaging but cannot confirm microbiological diagnosis.

High-yield TB recall:

Gold standard for TB diagnosis = Mycobacterial culture
Rapid diagnostic test = NAAT/GeneXpert

Exam pearl:
Definitive diagnosis of TB → Culture.

Medicine-02.question: ৪৪) Treatment duration of Continuation phase of Pulmonary Tuberculosis?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is 4 months. The standard treatment duration for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis is 6 months, consisting of a 2-month intensive phase followed by a 4-month continuation phase.

Standard TB regimen:

Intensive phase (2 months):

  • H – Isoniazid

  • R – Rifampicin

  • Z – Pyrazinamide

  • E – Ethambutol

Continuation phase (4 months):

  • H – Isoniazid

  • R – Rifampicin

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 2 months → Duration of intensive phase.

  • 6 months → Total treatment duration, not continuation phase.

  • 8 months → Not the standard duration for drug-sensitive pulmonary TB.

High-yield TB recall:

Pulmonary TB (drug-sensitive) = 2 months HRZE + 4 months HR

Exam pearl:
Continuation phase of pulmonary TB treatment = 4 months.

Medicine-02.question: ৪৫) Which anti-TB drug cause Peripheral neuropathy?
Medicine-02.exp: Explanation:

Medicine-02.question: ৪৬) Which anti-TB drug cause Hyperuricaemia?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is Pyrazinamide. Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricaemia by reducing renal excretion of uric acid, which may precipitate gout.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Isoniazid → Causes peripheral neuropathy and hepatitis.

  • Rifampicin → Causes orange discoloration of body fluids, hepatotoxicity, and drug interactions.

  • Streptomycin → Causes ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.

High-yield TB drug adverse effects:

Drug Important adverse effect
Isoniazid Peripheral neuropathy, hepatitis
Rifampicin Orange urine, CYP450 induction
Pyrazinamide Hyperuricaemia, hepatitis
Ethambutol Optic neuritis
Streptomycin Ototoxicity

Exam pearl:
Anti-TB drug causing hyperuricaemia = Pyrazinamide

Medicine-02.question: ৪৭) Which one is responsible for most common cause of death from cancer worldwide?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is lung cancer. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide due to its high incidence, aggressive nature, and late presentation.

Key points:

  • Most common cancer causing death worldwide → Lung cancer

  • Major risk factor → Cigarette smoking

  • Most common histological type → Adenocarcinoma (globally)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Breast cancer → Most commonly diagnosed cancer in women but not the leading cause of cancer death worldwide.

  • Ovarian cancer → Important cause of mortality among gynaecological cancers but less common overall.

  • Liver cancer → Major cause of cancer death, especially in regions with chronic hepatitis infection, but lower than lung cancer globally.

High-yield oncology recall:

Leading cause of cancer death worldwide = Lung cancer
Major risk factor = Smoking

Exam pearl:
Cancer mortality leader → Lung cancer.

Medicine-02.question: ৪৮) Which one is the most important cause of lung cancer?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is cigarette smoking. Smoking is the most important risk factor and the leading preventable cause of lung cancer.

Key points:

  • Responsible for the majority of lung cancer cases

  • Risk increases with:

    • Duration of smoking

    • Number of cigarettes smoked per day

    • Total pack-years

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Alcohol intake → Not a major independent cause of lung cancer.

  • Amphetamine → Not associated with lung cancer.

  • Occupational exposure → Important risk factor (e.g., asbestos, radon), but less significant than smoking.

High-yield oncology recall:

Most important cause of lung cancer = Cigarette smoking
Important occupational risks = Asbestos, radon, silica

Exam pearl:
Lung cancer → Strongest association = Cigarette smoking.

Medicine-02.question: ৪৯) Which one is the most common early symptom of lung cancer?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is cough. Persistent cough is the most common early symptom of lung cancer due to irritation or obstruction of the airways by the tumour.

Common symptoms of lung cancer:

  • Persistent cough (most common early symptom)

  • Haemoptysis

  • Breathlessness

  • Chest pain

  • Weight loss (usually later feature)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Weight loss → Common but usually occurs in advanced disease.

  • Haemoptysis → Important symptom but not the most common early symptom.

  • Breathlessness → Usually occurs later due to airway obstruction, pleural effusion, or advanced disease.

High-yield oncology recall:

Early symptom of lung cancer = Persistent cough
Red flag symptom = Haemoptysis

Exam pearl:
Most common presenting symptom of lung cancer = Cough.

Medicine-02.question: ৫০) The combination of absent breath sounds and a resonant percussion note is diagnostic of which of the following disease?
Medicine-02.exp:
The correct answer is pneumothorax. Absent breath sounds with a resonant (hyper-resonant) percussion note is a classic sign of air accumulation in the pleural space.

Clinical findings in pneumothorax:

  • ↓ or absent breath sounds

  • Hyper-resonant percussion note

  • Reduced chest expansion

  • Reduced vocal resonance

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Pneumonia → Causes bronchial breathing, increased vocal resonance, and dull percussion note.

  • Fibrosis → Causes fine crepitations and reduced breath sounds but not hyper-resonance.

  • Lung abscess → May cause bronchial breathing and a dull percussion note.

High-yield respiratory recall:

Pneumothorax = Air in pleural space → Hyper-resonance + Absent breath sounds

Exam pearl:
Absent breath sounds + hyper-resonant percussion = Pneumothorax.
